content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to use the internal real-time clock of [product_name] to control an output? I need the output to activate for about 10 minutes at the start of every hour.

Welcome to the forum. You can use eight weekly timers, each with three cams, or combine a weekly timer with an asynchronous pulse generator. Both approaches work correctly a day after starting [product_name]. Using just an asynchronous pulse generator will work immediately when [product_name] starts, but only at full hours. Refer to the attachment for three example configurations.

Thank you for the information. Could you explain why the timer functions only a day after starting [product_name]? Does that mean I have to wait a full day every time? If I power off the device, will I need to wait another day?
If you use eight weekly timers, the timer will activate every hour throughout the day.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for ways to trigger output signals for specific periods every hour using [product_name]'s internal clock. There is uncertainty about how timer functions behave, particularly after power cycles, and users are questioning whether scheduling causes delays or requires an entire day to function properly after restart.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the internal real-time clock to trigger outputs precisely each hour for a set duration, without significant delays, and for the scheduling to work immediately after the device restarts.
